region_name: Sol Duc, Seven Lakes Basin, High Divide & Lake Crescent
summary: The northwest high country of Olympic National Park: the Sol Duc valley (falls, hot springs, river and Deer Lake trails), the quota-managed Seven Lakes Basin and the High Divide crest with its face-to-face view of Mount Olympus, Heart Lake and Sol Duc Park, the Hoh Lake trail dropping to the Hoh River, Mink Lake and the Little Divide, Appleton Pass and the primitive Cat Basin way trails, plus the Lake Crescent day hikes and Aurora Ridge. The 18-19 mi High Divide loop (Sol Duc trailhead, Deer Lake, High Divide, Heart Lake, Sol Duc River) is the backbone; every camp is a designated, permit-reserved site, bear canisters are required for all overnight stays, and fires are banned above 3,500 ft. Distances are official/guidebook figures where they exist and OpenStreetMap-measured otherwise; elevations are USGS 3DEP samples unless a published figure is noted.

nodes.name: Sol Duc Trailhead
nodes.description: The road ends in a ring of giant trees, and the air already smells of wet moss and river spray. A wooden signboard lists names that sound like a promise: Sol Duc Falls, Deer Lake, High Divide.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: gravel lot edge, brown wooden trail-sign board and a small vault-toilet hut. Midground: wall of huge Douglas-fir and hemlock trunks in brown and dark green, moss dithered light green. Sky: only a narrow slot of light blue/white through the canopy. Landmark: the trail mouth as a dark arch between two trunks.

nodes.name: Mink Lake / Lover's Lane Trailhead
nodes.description: Behind the hot springs lodge, past the steam curling off the pools, a kiosk marks two paths: Lover's Lane, wandering upriver through the old trees, and the Mink Lake trail, climbing straight into the dark forest.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: kiosk with a little roof and a map; behind it a gated service road. Midground: two trail mouths diverging, one level (left), one climbing (right). Sky: gray-white dithered overcast. Landmark: wisps of white steam drifting from the pools at frame edge.

nodes.name: Sol Duc Hot Springs (in-game business name: The Steaming Fern Lodge)
nodes.description: Cabins, a little cafe and steaming mineral pools sit in a clearing by the river. After days on the trail, a soak here feels like being tucked into a warm blanket.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: rim of a blue-green pool with white steam dithers and a lifeguard chair. Midground: low brown cabins with green roofs. Background: dark forested ridges. Sky: pale gray-blue. Landmark: column of steam rising past the trees.

nodes.description: A big forest campground beside the river, with picnic tables, food lockers and the hush of water all night long.

nodes.name: Salmon Cascades

nodes.name: Sol Duc Falls
nodes.description: The river splits into white ribbons and pours sideways into a narrow, mossy slot, filling the air with cold mist and thunder. A wooden bridge crosses right above the roar, and an old trail shelter waits on the near bank.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: wooden footbridge railing in brown. Midground: dark rock slot with several white water ribbons, white/light-cyan dithered mist. Background: fern-draped walls in bright and dark green. Sky: canopy only. Landmark: bridge spanning the slot.

hazards.name: Steep snow on the High Divide and basin staircase
hazards.season: June to mid-July normally; any month after early storms.
hazards.real_world: NPS: steep slopes of the High Divide can stay snow- or ice-covered until mid-July or later; an ice axe and self-arrest skills are usually needed around Bogachiel Peak, along the Divide and into the basin when snow covers them.
hazards.game_event_idea: A tongue of hard morning snow slants across the trail above the basin. (A) Kick steps across now: 70% fine / 25% slip and scrape (lose 1 energy) / 5% slide into rocks (twisted knee, hike out, ranger may assist). Microspikes +15%, ice axe +15%, poles +5%. (B) Wait two hours for the sun to soften it: 95% safe but arrive late and roll for afternoon thunderstorms. (C) Take the lower Seven Lakes Basin route if it is clear. (D) Turn back to Deer Lake. (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Lightning and hail on the exposed High Divide
hazards.season: Mostly July to September afternoons.
hazards.real_world: Sept 5, 2026: thunder and heavy rain near Deer Lake and hail with lightning at Heart Lake; one party sheltered in dense trees for about an hour before continuing. Lightning also started a small fire on Sourdough Mountain (Aurora Ridge) on Aug 10, 2026.
hazards.game_event_idea: Thunder rumbles from the Hoh side while you are at the Potholes. (A) Wait in the trees an hour: 85% the storm passes, 15% it lingers and you camp late. (B) Push up onto the crest now: 60% you beat it / 30% soaked and chilled (need dry layers) / 10% caught in hail and lightning, forced retreat. (C) Change the plan and stay at Deer Lake: an off-permit night unless the permit says Deer Lake (3.7). (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Black bear feeding beside or on the trail
hazards.season: Late July to September (huckleberry/blueberry season); bears seen all summer.
hazards.real_world: 2026 reports: 4 to 11 bears per trip in August; a sow and cub split by the trail near the Bogachiel Peak spur; one bear about 30 ft away that ignored the hiker; another directly on the trail in fog.
hazards.game_event_idea: A bear is stripping berries 40 feet ahead and does not move. (A) Wait at a distance and talk calmly: 80% it ambles off in 10-20 minutes, 20% it stays (lose 30 min). (B) Make noise, wave poles, give a wide berth: 70% fine, 25% it bluffs and you back away, 5% you drop your pack (if food is not in a canister, bear gets a snack: trip ends early and the camp may close). (C) Go back to the last junction and take the other way (the basin or the crest). Never run. A mother with a cub doubles the waiting time. (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Bear visits camp at night
hazards.season: July to October.
hazards.real_world: July 2026: a bear circled a tent within about 20 ft at Heart Lake; Aug 2026: a hiker had a bear in her Lower Bridge Creek site and ate by the creek. Bear canisters are required for all overnight stays in the Olympic wilderness; hanging food is prohibited.
hazards.game_event_idea: Snuffling outside the tent at 2 am. If all food, trash and scented items (toothpaste, sunscreen, lip balm) are locked in the canister 100+ ft away: 95% the bear wanders off. If something scented is in the tent: 40% the bear paws the tent (gear damage), 10% it takes the item and the park later closes the camp. A ranger inspecting camps can cite an unlocked canister. An overnight with no canister at all is allowed (never a hard block): every night rolls a wildlife visitor (m1a_play_inputs.food_storage_visitors), a ranger who checks plays a ranger card, and lost food costs Leave No Trace. (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: No water on the High Divide crest
hazards.season: Late July to October (worst in heat waves).
hazards.real_world: 2026 reports: water stops at Deer Lake, then Lunch Lake (if you drop into the basin), then Heart Lake; one runner used about 1 L per hour in sun. NPS calls the Hoh Lake Trail hot and dry with little shade (1978 burn).
hazards.game_event_idea: Your bottles are getting light on the crest. Water capacity check: under 1.5 L carried = roll for "thirsty" (slower pace, headache 30%). Choice: drop 500 ft to Lunch Lake to refill (costs time and climbing) or ration to Heart Lake (60% fine / 40% headache and slower). Filter or tablets required to drink lake water safely. (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Mosquito and fly swarms at the lakes
hazards.season: Late June to early August; horse flies in August.
hazards.real_world: June-July 2026 reports: a "feeding frenzy" at Lunch Lake, Deer Lake buggy, mosquitoes "contenders" at Heart Lake; head nets and rain jackets made it fine. By late August most reports say no bugs.
hazards.game_event_idea: Dusk at the lake and the whine begins. With head net + repellent: no effect. Without: lose sleep (start tomorrow tired, -1 energy) 70% chance; or hide in the tent and miss the sunset. (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Hypothermia risk on a cold, wet, windy night
hazards.season: Any month; most common September-October and early season.
hazards.real_world: Sept 25-26, 2026: a party reached Appleton Pass in all-day rain with snow showers and howling wind; temperatures dropped below 30 F and with wet clothes it was very hard to stay warm. Early Sept 2026 mornings had frost in the basin.
hazards.game_event_idea: Rain turns to sleet as you reach camp and your sleeping bag is damp. Gear check: warm sleeping bag + dry base layer + tent = cold but OK. Missing two of those: 50% you shiver all night (-2 energy) and 15% you must descend at first light; missing all three: the Cold chain's first warning, with a sure choice on the page (dress, into the bag, a hot drink, or down at first light). Old School deaths come only at the chain's end, after its warnings (8.10, 9.5). (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Fog and unsigned junctions
hazards.season: Any time; marine fog common in summer.
hazards.real_world: 2026 reports: several intersections without signs (one party relied on an app), a summit user trail on Bogachiel Peak that was "much less friendly", and many days socked in on the Divide.
hazards.game_event_idea: Fog swallows the ridge at an unsigned fork. (A) Check map and compass/GPS: 95% right way. (B) Guess: 60% right / 40% you follow a user trail (lose 45 min, maybe a scramble). (C) Wait for a clearing: 50% it lifts within an hour. (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Knee-pounding stone steps and rocky descents
hazards.season: All season.
hazards.real_world: 2026 reports: the descent to Lunch Lake is "a knee buster" of staggered stone steps; the Sol Duc side descent has "relentless uneven stones"; one hiker sprained an ankle on the hike out.
hazards.game_event_idea: Steep rock steps, heavy pack. With trekking poles: 90% fine. Without: 75% fine / 20% sore knees (-1 energy tomorrow) / 5% rolled ankle (if first aid kit with wrap: limp out slowly; without: rescue call). (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Quota camps full / permit check
hazards.season: All reservation season; heaviest July-September weekends.
hazards.real_world: Permits are first-come on Recreation.gov from April 15; no walk-up sites are held. Oct 7, 2026 snapshot: Lunch Lake and Heart Lake had 0 group slots left. Rangers checked permits repeatedly in summer 2026 and asked campers without permits to leave; hikers must camp in the camp on their permit each night.
hazards.game_event_idea: At planning time, each camp and night rolls its quota (m1a_play_inputs.quota_availability, keyed by the trip seed, date and camp); full camps get alternates (river camps, Deer Lake). On the trail: on a legal night the permit check is a Director card (capped, 2.6); on an off-permit night a ranger roll is forced every night, uncapped, and plays the permit-check card when it hits (3.7, m1a_play_inputs.ranger_presence). A permit in order: a nod and a story. Wrong camp: a talking-to and maybe a walk to a legal camp at dusk. (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.game_event_idea: Arrive time choice: before 8 am = 95% park at the lot; 10 am-2 pm on a weekend = 70% walk up to a mile on the road. hazards.name: Fallen trees across the trail
hazards.season: Mostly early season after winter storms.
hazards.real_world: June 2026: five downed trees 1-4 ft diameter on the Sol Duc River Trail and blowdowns below Sol Duc Park; July 2026: one very large log in a Deer Lake Trail gulch with a hiker-made bypass. Rangers were clearing logs. Bogachiel River Trail (beyond little_divide) badly overgrown with large new blowdowns (June 2026).
hazards.game_event_idea: A giant log blocks the trail. (A) Climb over: 85% fine, 15% scraped shins/torn pants. (B) Crawl under with pack off: slower, 100% safe if gap exists. (C) Use the user bypass: 90% fine, small erosion guilt. (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Slippery rocks near Sol Duc Falls
hazards.season: Year-round; worst in high water and ice.
hazards.real_world: NPS asks visitors to view the falls only from designated viewing areas; leaving them can put you unexpectedly in the water. The 2013 park brochure asks parents to keep children under close supervision. Real incidents (park_rules.json search_and_rescue, waterfall_and_riverbank_falls): in June 2025 an 18-year-old died after crossing the upper river and going over the falls; in Sept 2019 a 15-year-old went over the falls and survived a rope rescue. This hazard is a real_incident site (GAME_DESIGN 9.5, principle 3): no death outcome may be built from it; the falls get the stay-on-trail mechanic instead.
hazards.game_event_idea: A photo from past the railing tempts. (A) Stay on the bridge and the overlook: sure. (B) Step past the viewing area onto the mossy rock: a ranger's line and a Leave No Trace cost. The page never builds a fall from it: this is a real_incident site (9.5), so the falls get the stay-on-trail mechanic only. (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: River crossing on a high footlog/bridge
hazards.season: All season; slick when wet or icy.
hazards.real_world: WTA describes crossing the Sol Duc River on a footlog high above the water; a June 2026 report describes a large old footbridge. Generally straightforward.
hazards.game_event_idea: Wet, mossy planks over white water. Normal pace: 97% fine, 3% slip and bruise (poles reduce to 1%). (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Day hikers caught out by darkness on the loop
hazards.season: All season; worst in September-October with shorter days.
hazards.real_world: Aug 2026: a hiker passed at 6 pm with 8 miles still to go; many day hikers attempt the 18-19 mi loop.
hazards.game_event_idea: If you chose "day hike" for an 18-mile loop: each hour of late start adds 15% chance of finishing in the dark. With headlamp: slow but fine. Without: 50% stumble (minor injury), 20% need help from passing backpackers (they share a light and trail mix). (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Exposed rock and hiker-placed ropes above the Storm King trail
hazards.season: All season; deadly when wet.
hazards.real_world: Beyond the end of the maintained trail the climbers' route is unmaintained and exposed; ropes are not installed or maintained by the park. In November 2017 a 21-year-old hiker died after a loose rock gave way and he fell; search and rescue calls are not uncommon.
hazards.game_event_idea: You reach the sign. (A) Turn around and enjoy the view through the trees: 100% safe. (B) Use the frayed ropes to the rock knob: 85% amazing view / 12% scary moment / 3% a fall whose worst outcome is Serious (a sprained wrist and a rescue). Storm King is a real_incident area, so no death outcome is built there (9.5). Rain doubles the bad outcomes. (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Steep landslide crossing on Pyramid Peak
hazards.season: Year-round; worse after heavy rain.
hazards.real_world: NPS: one section of the Pyramid Peak trail crosses a steep landslide.
hazards.game_event_idea: Loose gully across the trail. Careful crossing 92% fine / 8% slide a few feet (scrapes). Poles help. (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Cold, deep water at Lake Crescent and Devil's Punchbowl
hazards.season: Year-round.
hazards.real_world: NPS: the lake is very cold and deep; always wear a life jacket on the water. Official max depth 624 ft (a 2013-14 survey found 596 ft).
hazards.game_event_idea: Other swimmers are jumping into the Punchbowl. (A) Watch: sure. (B) Jump: 80% gasping-cold joy / 20% cold shock and a struggle to the rocks (a bystander helps; spirits and energy cost). (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Hot, dry, brushy Hoh Lake Trail
hazards.season: July-September.
hazards.real_world: NPS: very strenuous, little canopy (1978 Hoh Fire area), carry plenty of water; 22 switchbacks. Sept 2026: wet brush soaked shoes on a misty morning.
hazards.game_event_idea: Climbing out of the Hoh at noon. Water < 2 L: 50% heat exhaustion warning (rest 1 hour). Morning brush: no gaiters/rain pants = wet feet (blister roll 30%). (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Cougar sign near Deer Lake
hazards.season: Any season.
hazards.real_world: June 2026: a shredded, half-eaten deer carcass near the Deer Lake campsites; Sept 2026: large scat that hikers guessed was from a big cat. Encounters are rare.
hazards.game_event_idea: You find a cached deer carcass beside the trail. (A) Leave quickly, big and loud: sure. (B) Linger for a photo: 10% a low growl and a slow backing away (a tense page, always survivable). (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Campfire rules and seasonal bans
hazards.season: Fires are never allowed above 3,500 ft; below it, seasonal bans apply on their own dates (2026: conditions_2026; future summers: park_rules.json campfires.future_ban_climatology).
hazards.real_world: Fires are prohibited above 3,500 ft and at all High Divide/basin camps; below that line only in existing rings with dead and down wood, and not at all during seasonal bans. Stoves allowed if 3 ft from vegetation.
hazards.game_event_idea: The player packed only a fire-starter plan for cooking. At a lake camp: no fire allowed - eat cold food (morale -1) unless a stove was packed. At a river camp below 3,500 ft in a non-ban month: small fire allowed (morale +1); during a ban (its dates from the conditions overlay; future summers drawn from park_rules.json campfires.future_ban_climatology) a lit fire brings a ranger card and Leave No Trace -20. (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: End of season: early snow and closing permits
hazards.season: Late September to October.
hazards.real_world: Seven Lakes Basin/High Divide online reservations end Oct 15 (2026); after that, permits only via the WIC. A dusting of snow coated trees and peaks on Sept 25-26, 2026. Sol Duc Road is often closed by snow and ice in winter.
hazards.game_event_idea: October trip: roll weather. 60% crisp blue fall colors, 30% cold rain, 10% first snow on the Divide (turn back at Potholes unless microspikes + warm gear). (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Narrow, eroded primitive and way trails
hazards.season: Mid-July to September.
hazards.real_world: July 2026: a hiker turned around 0.1 mi short of Swimming Bear Lake on a narrow, eroded tread; Sept 2026: Spread Eagle Pass way trail beautiful but steep with some bushwhacking. NPS: some Aurora Ridge sections are hard to follow.
hazards.game_event_idea: The path narrows to a boot-width ledge across steep heather. Full pack: (A) drop the pack and scout: 90% fine; (B) push on: 75% fine / 20% slide a few feet (scrapes) / 5% turn back; (C) turn around. (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Getting there: US 101 Hoh River Bridge closures and ferries
hazards.season: Whenever the conditions overlay lists a road or bridge closure on the trip's dates (2026: the US 101 Hoh River Bridge windows in conditions_2026).
hazards.real_world: WSDOT closed the US 101 Hoh River Bridge south of Forks 24 hours a day in three 6-day windows for emergency repairs; the only detour is about 4 hours around Hood Canal. Matters for shuttles between the Sol Duc and the Hoh or for drivers coming from the coast.
hazards.game_event_idea: Planning screen event: if the trip is a Sol Duc-to-Hoh traverse in a closure window, the shuttle driver must take the 4-hour detour (+1 day) or the player picks another exit.

hazards.name: Mice and jays raid snacks
hazards.season: All season.
hazards.real_world: WTA notes the old Mink Lake shelter is home to rodents; Canada jays and chipmunks are bold at popular camps; a 2026 hiker lost car snacks to a mouse at the Sol Duc trailhead.
hazards.game_event_idea: Lunch break: a gray jay lands on your boot. (A) Shoo it and pack food away: fine. (B) Toss it a crumb: it takes the crumb, then 50% the rest of the sandwich (feeding wildlife: Leave No Trace -10). (Percentages are suggested design odds, not real-world statistics.)

wildlife_and_plants.name: American black bear
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Very common in late summer berry season; 2026 trip reports logged up to 11 sightings per trip. Usually indifferent if given space. Canisters protect both bears and hikers.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Hazard and moment. On the trail, a bear in the huckleberries ahead: wait, detour or make noise, never run. At dusk, a bear grazing a far meadow is a quiet Look. At camp, a closed canister 100 ft away means the bear walks on; food left out makes it a food thief that remembers (8.10). No wildlife card has a fatal branch (9.5).

wildlife_and_plants.name: Roosevelt elk
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Herds summer in the high meadows; bulls bugle in September (heard from the Divide in Sept 2026). NPS notes elk are frequently seen along the Hoh Lake Trail.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Moment: a bull's bugle rising from the Hoh valley at dawn in September, as a sound cue and a Look. In the rut (mid-September on), a bull near the trail is a give-it-a-wide-berth card.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Columbian black-tailed deer
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Does and fawns common in camps; they seek salt from urine, so pee on rocks away from tents and plants.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Moment and nuisance: a doe and fawn crossing camp at dusk (a Look). Deer chew salty gear left out (a sweaty hip belt, pole grips); pee on rock away from camp.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Olympic marmot
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Endemic to the Olympic Mountains; lives in subalpine meadows and talus; whistles an alarm. Seen near Swimming Bear Lake and along the Divide in 2026.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Moment: a marmot sunning on a warm boulder, and its alarm whistle across the talus as a sound cue (it is the marmots' business, not a warning to the hiker). The bold marmot that goes for salty gear is a Larry card from M1b (2.6).

wildlife_and_plants.name: Cougar (mountain lion)
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Rarely seen; sign such as a cached deer carcass reported near Deer Lake in June 2026.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Hazard, by sign only: tracks or an old cached carcass near Deer Lake. A rare, tense page with a sure choice to leave; always survivable. The ranger's advice goes in a Ranger's Note.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Mountain goat
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Not native to the Olympics; most were captured and relocated or removed 2018-2020 because they damaged fragile plants (the 2018 Seven Lakes Basin administrative closure was announced with no reason given in the release). A few may remain.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: History, not a trail encounter: a ranger line or Look about why the goats are almost gone (removed 2018-2022). At most a very rare distant sighting.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Canada jay (gray jay)
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Bold "camp robber" that lands near lunch spots; feeding wildlife is prohibited.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Food thief: lands beside a lunch spot and takes whatever is left unattended. Feeding it is prohibited (Leave No Trace -10); shooing it and packing the food away is the sure choice.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Sooty grouse
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Seen in the meadows (2025-2026 reports); males hoot deeply in early summer.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Moment: a hen and chicks crossing the trail, or a male's deep hoot in early summer as a sound cue.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Hermit thrush and varied thrush
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Ethereal forest songs heard in June 2026 reports; varied thrush has a single buzzy whistle.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Sound: the hermit thrush's flute and the varied thrush's single buzzy note in the forest scenes (PC-speaker chirps).

wildlife_and_plants.name: Coho and Chinook salmon
wildlife_and_plants.notes: NPS: Chinook and coho ascend the Sol Duc in late summer and spawn in late fall; coho leap at Salmon Cascades in autumn; the Sol Duc has salmon in every season.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Moment: coho leaping at Salmon Cascades, a drive-in stop in autumn.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Brook trout
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Caught in Deer Lake in 2026; not native to the high lakes. No fishing license needed in the park (park regulations still apply).
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Moment: trout rising on Deer Lake at dusk. With a rod packed, a quiet evening page that lifts spirits (no license needed in the park). Nothing in the food plan depends on it.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Mosquitoes, deer flies and horse flies
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Heavy late June-July; mostly gone by late August.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Hazard: late June to early August at the lakes. A head net and repellent keep the evening; without them, lost sleep, or the tent and a missed sunset.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Avalanche lily
wildlife_and_plants.notes: White lilies in carpets right after snowmelt; June 2026 "avalanche lily explosion" from Deer Lake along the ridge to Sol Duc Park. NPS mentions them on the Hoh Lake Trail.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Scenery: carpets of white lilies right behind the melting snow, in early-season scenes (late June and July; earlier in a low-snow year).

wildlife_and_plants.name: Glacier lily
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Yellow lily that blooms at the very edge of melting snow; a June 2026 hiker said the glacier lilies "put on a show" near the Divide.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Scenery: yellow lilies at the edge of melting snow on the Divide early in the season, named in a Look. It is not the Bonfire Lily, which is invented (GAME_DESIGN 10.2).

wildlife_and_plants.name: Piper's bellflower
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Blue bellflower endemic to the Olympic Mountains, growing in dry rock crevices in subalpine/alpine zones, blooming July-August. Presence specifically on the High Divide is not confirmed.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Scenery and a Look line: an Olympic endemic in rock crevices high up, one of the real flowers a lily book's back cover names (10.2). Never picked; there is nothing to collect.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Pink mountain heather
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Common subalpine shrub with pink bell flowers in July.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Scenery: ground texture of the subalpine scenes. The meadows are fragile, so a shortcut across them costs Leave No Trace.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Magenta paintbrush, broadleaf lupine, Sitka valerian, subalpine fleabane, shooting star
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Peak meadow bloom July to early August (June in low-snow 2026).
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Scenery: the July meadow palette for Sol Duc Park, Heart Lake and the crest.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Huckleberries and blueberries
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Ripe August to early September; draw bears; hikers in 2026 made "blueberry tea". Done by late September.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Moment and hazard: berries lift spirits on a snack page (August to early September) and draw bears to the same slopes.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Bunchberry, queen's cup, northwest twayblade, Pacific coralroot
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Forest-floor flowers and small orchids noted in June 2026.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Scenery: forest-floor flowers in the June forest scenes.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Devil's club and skunk cabbage
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Spiny devil's club in wet forest; skunk cabbage in boggy spots (reported growing in the tread on the Bogachiel side).
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Hazard texture: grabbing devil's club for balance after a slip hurts (a small cost); skunk cabbage marks wet tread.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Douglas-fir, western hemlock, western redcedar, Pacific silver fir
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Never-logged old growth along the Sol Duc River Trail and around Lake Crescent.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Scenery: the giant trunks of the falls and river scenes, and the deep canopy that brings trail-dark early (7.2).

wildlife_and_plants.name: Mountain hemlock, subalpine fir, Alaska yellow-cedar
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Subalpine trees forming parkland clumps above about 4,000 ft.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Scenery: parkland silhouettes in the ridge scenes.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Wooly chanterelle, coral fungus, hawk's wing
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Noted on an Aug 2026 trip; late summer and fall.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Scenery in late-summer forest scenes. Never eaten in the game.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Dog vomit slime mold
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Actually a slime mold, not a fungus; a bright yellow blob on wood (Aug 2026 report).
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: A Look line: the bright yellow blob on a log that is neither plant nor fungus.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Old man's beard / witch's hair lichens and lettuce lungwort
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Hanging lichens and leafy lungwort festoon old-growth branches in this wet forest.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Scenery: hanging lichen, dithered, in the old-growth scenes.

permit_and_rules.rule: A wilderness permit is required for every overnight stay in the Olympic wilderness, year-round, reserved on Recreation.gov (permit 4098362); no self-registration at trailheads and no walk-up sites held. Permits are issued by WIC staff 3 days before the trip and printed by the permit holder.

Fees: $6 non-refundable reservation fee per permit plus $8 per person per night for ages 16+; $45 Annual Wilderness Pass covers the nightly fee (not the $6). Park entrance fee is separate. Permit holder must be 16+; under-16s free but count toward group size.

Summer-season reservations (May 15-Oct 15) open April 15 at 7 AM Pacific. Seven Lakes Basin/High Divide reservation season Jul 15-Oct 15, 2026; dates outside that window by contacting the WIC (360-565-3100).

Quota area: Sol Duc/Seven Lakes Basin and Hoh Lake. You must camp in the camp reserved for that night; itinerary changes must be made on Recreation.gov or at a WIC before the trip unless approved by a ranger.

Per-night quotas (Recreation.gov, Oct 2026): Deer Lake 10 groups/26 people; Lunch Lake 9/28; Heart Lake 5/26; Sol Duc Park 4/18; Hoh Lake 4/14; Sol Duc Falls 3/18; Mink Lake 3/18; Potholes 2/12; Lower Bridge Creek 2/12; single-group sites (6 people): Canyon Creek #1-#3, Sol Duc River #1-#4, Appleton Junction, Rocky Creek, Sol Duc Crossing, Round Lake, Clear Lake, Heart Lake Junction Camp; group sites (7-12): Deer Lake, Sol Duc Park, Seven Mile, C.B. Flats; Horse Head stock camp 10 people/8 stock.

Maximum group size 12 people (8 stock) anywhere; most Sol Duc/Seven Lakes Basin/Hoh Lake camps cap groups at 6, so groups of 7-12 must use designated group sites. Affiliated groups may not combine above 12 and must camp and travel at least 1 mile apart.

All food, garbage and scented items must be stored in a park-approved bear canister for any overnight stay in the Olympic wilderness; hanging food (bear wires or self-made hangs) is prohibited; Ursacks/odor bags not accepted. Canisters can be borrowed free at the Port Angeles WIC (first come, first served).

Campfires are prohibited above 3,500 ft (all High Divide, basin, Heart Lake, Sol Duc Park, Deer Lake, Hoh Lake camps). Below 3,500 ft (river camps, Canyon Creek, Sol Duc Falls, Mink Lake) fires only in established rings with dead and down wood, and never during seasonal bans.

2026: Stage 2 fire restrictions from Aug 7, 2026 (date per the Olympic NF order; NPS releases of Aug 11 and Aug 26 confirm it was in effect) prohibit all campfires in Olympic National Park and Olympic National Forest; stoves allowed 3 ft from vegetation. Still in effect in the Aug 26, 2026 release; no lifting notice found by Oct 7.

Use toilets where provided (Deer Lake, Lunch Lake, Heart Lake, Sol Duc Park, Hoh Lake composting toilet, C.B. Flats); do not urinate in them. Elsewhere bury waste 6-8 in deep and 200 ft from water, camps and trails; pack out toilet paper. Urinate on rocks or trail, not plants.
Camp only in designated sites in the Sol Duc/Seven Lakes Basin area; stay on trails because meadows are extremely fragile.
Pets and bicycles are prohibited on park trails, except leashed pets and bikes on the Spruce Railroad Trail. No backpacking with a dog anywhere in the park.
Stock: Horse Head and Deer Lake stock sites (NPS trail pages say llamas only); Appleton Pass Trail is day-use only for stock; max 8 stock per group.
Cancellation: cancel 3 or more full days before the start date for a refund (the $6 fee is non-refundable); no-shows forfeit all fees. Changes possible until the permit is issued.
Treat all drinking water (boil, filter or chemical) to prevent Giardia.
No fishing license is required in Olympic National Park (park fishing regulations still apply).
Drones (unmanned aircraft) are prohibited; firearm discharge prohibited.

Camps not shown on the online map (cross-country areas and hidden camps such as Long Lake, Morgenroth Lake, Lake #8, Sol Duc Lake, Swimming Bear Lake, Cat Basin, Bruce's Roost, Haigs Lake, Hidden Lake, Little Divide, Eagle Lakes) must be arranged through the WIC.
Aurora Ridge: campsites anywhere off vegetation and at least 200 ft from water; bear canisters required; fires prohibited above 3,500 ft.

uncertain_claims: Segment distances disagree among sources: NPS High Divide loop 18.2 mi, WTA 19 mi, 2026 hiker GPS 18-22.6 mi. This file uses WTA/NPS anchors (trailhead-Appleton junction 4.9, Sol Duc Park 7.0, Heart Lake 8.0, High Divide junction 8.4; falls-Deer Lake 2.9) and OSM-measured distances elsewhere, giving an 18.4 mi loop.
Sol Duc Falls to Deer Lake: NPS 2013 brochure 3.0 mi (3.8 from trailhead), WTA 2.9, OSM 2.7, NPS 2019 GIS 2.4. Used 2.9.
Lunch Lake spur: NPS High Divide page says 0.5 mi; NPS GIS (0.85) and OSM (0.84) both measure about 0.8 mi. Used 0.9 total (0.5 + 0.4) from the rim junction.

Hoh Lake Trail length: WTA and OSM give 4.7 mi junction-to-lake; NPS figures (Hoh Lake 14.7 mi from Hoh trailhead, 9.7 from Sol Duc trailhead, junction to Bogachiel Peak junction 6.4 mi) imply about 5.0-5.2. Used 4.7. NPS 9.7 mi from Sol Duc trailhead vs this graph 9.0 mi. [Fact check 2026-10-08: switched to the NPS-consistent 4.5 mi junction-to-C.B. Flats (5.0 mi to Hoh Lake), so Hoh Lake is 14.7 mi from the Hoh trailhead as NPS states.]
Potholes camp: Recreation.gov says 3/4 mile above Deer Lake; OSM measures 1.0 mi. Used 1.0.
Mink Lake to Little Divide junction: OSM 1.8 mi; NPS (Deer Lake 8 mi via Mink Lake) implies about 2.0 mi. NPS lists the loop as 11 mi while The Mountaineers list 13.6 mi; this graph gives 13.6 mi.

Mount Storm King: NPS trail page says 1.7 mi to 2,700 ft (from the Marymere junction); NPS brochure 2.2 mi one way and 2,000 ft gain; WTA 4.0 mi round trip, high point 2,600 ft. True summit elevation given as 4,534, 4,537 or 4,538 ft; distance from the end of maintained trail to the rope viewpoints is unverified.
Aurora Creek Trail: NPS 3.4 mi and 3,220 ft gain; DEM at the OSM-mapped junction suggests about 3,500 ft net. aurora_creek_junction elevation (4,150 ft) is a DEM sample at the OSM location.

Elevations are USGS 3DEP point samples at OSM/NPS coordinates and may differ from signed or map values by tens of feet (e.g., Bogachiel Peak DEM 5,463 vs published 5,474/5,478; Mount Olympus DEM 7,928 vs official 7,980). Sol Duc Park published figures vary (~4,000-4,200).
Segment gains/losses are DEM-derived (40 m sampling, smoothed, 30 ft hysteresis) except where a published figure is cited; expect +/-10-15%.

Canyon Creek #1-#3 positions: OSM tags place #3 near 3,370 ft (consistent with Recreation.gov's 3,500 ft note) while the 2018 NPS camp KML places all three within 0.7 mi near 2,650-2,950 ft. OSM positions used.
Recreation.gov division coordinates for Sol Duc camps are wrong (projected values in the lat/lon fields); NPS KML and OSM coordinates used instead.

Hidden camps (Long Lake, Morgenroth Lake, Lake #8, Sol Duc Lake, Swimming Bear Lake, Cat Basin, Cat Basin Stock Camp, Bruce's Roost, Haigs Lake, Silver Snag, Blackwood Lake, Hidden Lake, Little Divide, Deer Lake Llama Site, Eagle Lakes, Aurora Springs, Pyramid Peak, Barnes Creek Trail) exist in the permit system but are not bookable online; whether they are currently open, and their exact locations (Lake #8, Silver Snag, Aurora Springs), could not be verified.

Off-trail segments (Clear Lake-Long Lake-Sol Duc Lake-Morgenroth-Y Lake-No Name Lake, Swimming Bear-Haigs Lake, Little Divide-Blackwood Lake, last ~0.5 mi to Hidden Lake) use straight-line map distance and net elevation only; real routes are longer and may be impractical.

Appleton Pass camp rules conflict: Recreation.gov division text says bear wire or canister and "use available toilet"; park-wide 2026 rules require canisters and the NPS Appleton page says no toilets. Hoh Lake: older NPS map data says bear wire, 2026 Recreation.gov says canisters only. [Fact check 2026-10-08: the NPS Appleton Pass page says 'Toilet Facilities: None' and campfires are prohibited at Appleton Pass/Oyster Lake. Toilet set to false in both region files.]
The NPS Appleton Pass and Hoh Lake pages say canisters are "recommended" in one section and required in another; 2026 permit text (required everywhere) used.
Campfire ban status after Aug 26, 2026 not confirmed; bans have been lifted in mid-September in past years.
Eagle Ranger Station location and 2026 staffing not verified (coordinates left null).
Lake Crescent lodge area node coordinates left null (exact building location not verified); business names are fictional in-game.
Mirror Lake is an unofficial name used on OSM and by hikers; Morgenroth Lake is the GNIS spelling (the task brief spelled it Morganroth).
GNIS names the ridge near the Mink Lake/Little Divide area "Low Divide" (Clallam County); the trail is the Little Divide Trail. Do not confuse with the shared node low_divide (Elwha/Quinault).
Piper's bellflower presence on the High Divide/Bogachiel Peak is not confirmed; it is documented elsewhere in the Olympics.
Landslide near the Lunch Lake descent (Sept 2026) and the dead bear in Hoh Lake (late Sept 2026) come from single trip reports with no NPS confirmation.
Lake Crescent maximum depth: official 624 ft; a 2013-14 survey measured 596 ft.
Sol Duc hot springs pool session prices in 2026 sources range $18-$20 per 90-minute adult session.
Drive times are OSRM free-flow estimates and ignore entrance-station waits, construction and parking time.
NPS Mink Lake page lists an elevation range of 1,100-4,130 ft, but the resort trailhead is about 1,650 ft (WTA/DEM).
Hiking Project and some maps place the Sol Duc River Trail/High Divide junction next to Heart Lake rather than on the ridge.

Cross-region overlap: the Hoh region file also has a hoh_lake_trail_junction -> c_b_flats_group_site segment (4.5 mi, +3,484/-406 ft) while this file has c_b_flats_group_site -> hoh_lake_trail_junction 4.2 mi (WTA/OSM-based). Keep one at merge time; the hoh_lake_trail_junction stub here copies the Hoh region coordinates/elevation (1,013 ft). [RESOLVED by fact check 2026-10-08: both copies are now 4.5 mi, +90/-3,160 ft in this direction. That figure follows NPS: Hoh Lake 14.7 mi from the Hoh trailhead, and junction to Bogachiel Peak junction now totals NPS's 6.4 mi. C.B. Flats elevation is 4,091 ft in both files.]

quota_availability.what: The chance a solo party finds a site left at a camp for a night when the permit is planned. Group and stock sites are never offered (camp.group_site, camp.stock_site).
quota_availability.roll_key: hash(trip seed, date, camp). The seed is drawn at Begin a new book, so the planning draws are fixed for the book; changing the date re-rolls the camp; Try this trip again copies the stamped permit (lead call 8).
quota_availability.night_types: weekend = Friday and Saturday nights; midweek = Sunday to Thursday nights. Labor Day weekend's Saturday and Sunday nights use half the weekend value.
quota_availability.months: Jul is the online window from Jul 15; Oct runs to Oct 15. Sep and Oct are no easier on weekends than Aug by much (the 2026-10-07 snapshot was full midweek).

desk_requests.what: WIC-only camps the ranger may grant at the desk: park_rules.json permits.desk_requests (70% midweek, 40% weekends, keyed by trip seed, date and camp). M1a offers Bruce's Roost, Cat Basin and Hidden Lake; Long Lake and Sol Duc Lake (off trail) and the Morgenroth phone call wait for M1b (lead call 1).

camp_evening_visit.what: The chance a ranger walks through a camp on a given evening; weekend here means Friday, Saturday and Sunday nights (rangers work the busy nights). A meadow night off any site uses the nearest camp's value.

permit_check.legal_night: The permit check is a Director Larry card, at most one a day and two a book (2.6, 8.4); its deal weight on a night is that camp's evening-visit chance.
permit_check.off_permit_night: Forced and uncapped: every off-permit night rolls the camp's evening-visit chance, and a hit plays the permit-check card (lead call 5; 3.7). The Leave No Trace cost is charged whether or not a ranger comes.
permit_check.after_a_citation: The next permit check in the same region is 1.5 times as likely (9.8; estimate).

on_trail.what: Rangers met per hour on each trail section (sections below), at midday; evenings use 0.4 times. Feeds the Larry odds: 1 - exp(-rate x hours) is the chance a ranger strolls by (2.6: about 12% on a Saturday afternoon on the crest, 3-4% on a weekday evening).

trail_traffic.what: Other parties met per hour on each section at midday on an August day: kind strangers (9.2, 'Ask for help', base 70% once someone is there), full camps, and how likely a Boy is (7.11). Met parties follow a Poisson process: P(at least one in t hours) = 1 - exp(-rate x hour factor x month factor x weather factor x t).

food_storage_visitors.what: The nightly wildlife-visitor roll when food is not in a closed canister 100 ft from the tent: no canister at all (allowed, never a hard block: lead call 4), food that didn't fit, or a can left open. Visitors are mice, jays, deer and, now and then, a bear; habituated camps are worse.

p_bear_given_visitor.note: Berry season (late July to September) brings bears to Heart Lake, Lunch Lake, Deer Lake, Sol Duc Park and Hoh Lake (2026 reports, hazard bear_in_camp).

food_storage_visitors.with_canister_closed: Food in a closed canister 100 ft away: visitors x 0.15 (crumbs and a curious nose), and nothing is lost.
food_storage_visitors.consequences: Food lost to wildlife costs Leave No Trace -15 (9.6); a ranger who checks plays a ranger card; a bear that gets food makes the next bear in this region bolder (9.8).

places.what: Overlay fields per place (E.5) for the loop's 47 nodes.

fields.map_xy: Map position in tenths of a mile, x east and y south of 47.955 N, 123.84 W (computed from lat and lon). The map screen scales it.
fields.canopy: Share of the sky the trees block, 0 to 1 (estimate): sets trail-dark (7.2) and how much rain and sun reach the hiker.
fields.cold_pool: true for basins, lake hollows and meadows where cold air pools on clear nights (-4 F, 7.5).
fields.water: Water at the place in August and September: sure, likely, unverified (the research couldn't confirm late-summer water), near (a short walk), river (a river beside a trailhead or junction), none.
fields.views: What a Look from here can see; view_score 0-3 drives the landmark-view points (9.6) and the scene composer's backdrop (11.7).
fields.traffic_section: The trail_traffic section a place belongs to.
fields.snow_feature: The Bonfire Lily's snow feature (10.2): windows are the doc's design estimates, shifted by snow year. M1b.
fields.bonfire_lily_weight: 0 everywhere in M1a (the lily arrives in M1b); from M1b, 1 where a snow feature is in sight.
